PLAN "4-Week On-Ramp Block: Postpartum 10wks (Home, light dumbbells)"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Postpartum reconditioning and gradual loading"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 30m "Acclimatisation Session 1":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          dumbbell_row 2x10 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          goblet_squat 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_press 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 30m "Acclimatisation Session 2":
        warmup:
          marching 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hip_thrust 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          Romanian_deadlift 2x10 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          lateral_raise 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_flexor_stretch 2 minutes
      DAY Friday training 30m "Acclimatisation Session 3":
        warmup:
          jogging_in_place 3 minutes
          shoulder_mkre 2 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          step_up 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          push_up 2x8..12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          bent_over_row 2x10 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          overhead_stretch 3 minutes
    WEEK 2:
      DAY Monday training 35m "Foundation Build 1":
        warmup:
          walking 6 minutes
          scapular_retraction 1 minute
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 3x12 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x10 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
          incline_press 3x10 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
        cooldown:
          hamstring_stretch 2 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 35m "Foundation Build 2":
        warmup:
          march_in_place 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hip_thrust 3x12 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
          romanian_deadlift 3x10 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
          lateral_raise 3x12 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 2 minutes
      DAY Friday training 35m "Foundation Build 3":
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          step_up 3x10 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
          push_up 3x8..12 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
          cable_row 3x10 rpe 6 rest 75 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 2 minutes
    WEEK 3:
      DAY Monday training 40m "Progression Phase 1A":
        warmup:
          brisk_walk 6 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 3x12 rpe 6 rest 70 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x12 rpe 6 rest 70 seconds
          incline_press 3x10 rpe 6 rest 70 seconds
          face_pull 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_flexor_stretch 2 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 40m "Progression Phase 1B":
        warmup:
          marching 6 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hip_thrust 3x12 rpe 6 rest 70 seconds
          romanian_deadlift 3x10 rpe 6 rest 70 seconds
          reverse_plank 2x20s rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          glute_stretch 2 minutes
      DAY Friday training 40m "Progression Phase 1C":
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 6 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          step_up 3x12 rpe 6 rest 70 seconds
          dumbbell_press 3x10 rpe 6 rest 70 seconds
          bent_over_row 3x12 rpe 6 rest 70 seconds
        cooldown:
          thoracic_rotation 2 minutes
    WEEK 4:
      DAY Monday training 45m "Load Tolerance & Prep for Jump-Restriction End":
        warmup:
          brisk_walk 6 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 4x10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_row 4x8..12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          incline_press 4x8..12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          calf_stretch 2 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 45m "Stability & Mobility Focus":
        warmup:
          dynamic_series 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hip_thrust 3x12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          dead_bug 3x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          side_plank 2x20s per side
        cooldown:
          cat_cow 2 minutes
      DAY Friday training 45m "Volume Build with Low Impact":
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 6 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          step_up 4x10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          push_up 4x8..12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          cable_row 4x10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 2 minutes

Notes:
- Exercises restricted to canonical names only.
- No jumping exercises prescribed (per postpartum ramp). If any session ideas include jumping, substitute with low-impact option like step_up or march-in-place variations.
- Warmups and cooldowns use cardio modalities from: walking (represented via walking), jogging alternatives are represented as jog_in_place or marching; for true cardio, you can swap in running after clearance, but here kept moderate; you can adjust durations if needed.
- RPE targets are 5–6 for acclimatisation to moderate loading; progress to 6–7 as tolerated in Weeks 2–4.
- Reps notations follow 3x10 or 3x8..12 with rpe <appropriate>. All sets are listed before reps in each line.
- If you need to adjust due to fatigue or soreness, reduce volume by dropping a set per exercise in a given week.

PLAN "Diastasis Screening & Monitoring Plan for 4-Week On-Ramp Block: Postpartum 10wks"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Monitor abdominal separation and progressive loading"

PHASES
  PHASE "Screening Phase" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 10m "Screening Briefing & Setup":
        warmup:
          walking 3 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          diastasis_self_screen 1x1 rpe 1
        notes:
          - In this session, the trainer guides the client through a self-check for diastasis recti using a gentle, non-load bearing method: lift head and shoulders off floor in hook-lying, palpate linea alba for separation width and depth, hold for 5 seconds, observe doming or coning.
          - If separation is >2.5 cm (or client reports doming, gap visible at rest), flag for modification and consult clinician. If uncertain, document as screen pending clinician assessment.
    WEEK 2:
      DAY Wednesday training 10m "Form & Palpation Check":
        core:
          diastasis_palpation_technique 1x1 rpe 1
        notes:
          - Reassess at rest and with gentle curl (no loaded flexion). Record client feedback on abdomen function, rib flare, and pelvic floor comfort.
    WEEK 3:
      DAY Friday training 10m "Progressive Symptom Inquiry":
        core:
          symptom_log 1x1 rpe 1
        notes:
          - Ask about symptoms: linea alba tension, bulge with exertion, leakage, back pain. If any bulge with simple task, consider decline in loading or seek medical clearance.
    WEEK 4:
      DAY Monday training 10m "Clinical Referral Thresholds":
        notes:
          - If self-screening indicates notable diastasis (>2 cm) or symptoms worsen, arrange referral to physical therapist with experience in postpartum rehab.
          - Document plan: maintain low-load anti-flexion core, monitor symptoms, progress only with clinician clearance.

PHASE ALL weeks:
  NOTES:
    - The main on-ramp continues; core program remains anti-flexion/anti-rotation as previously prescribed.
    - Provide education: avoid traditional crunches, avoid full abdominal bracing that increases intra-abdominal pressure during early progressions.
    - If a clinician confirms diastasis, adjust: avoid loaded spinal flexion, reduce intra-abdominal pressure movements, and progress with gentle core work as advised.
    - Track diastasis status alongside training load (RPE, sets, reps). Update plan if width remains or increases.

EQUIPMENT
  - No additional equipment needed beyond home dumbbells; can use bodyweight for screening demonstration.

Notes:
- This document adds a structured screening protocol within the 4-week plan; it does not replace medical diagnosis.
- The screening moves are non-invasive and can be performed by the client with coach guidance.
- All terms use canonical WPL-AI vocabulary; no new exercise names introduced for screening beyond diastasis_screen related items.

PLAN "4-Week Return-to-Fitness Summary Plan" 
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Condensed summary of Phase 1: 4-week postpartum on-ramp with anti-flexion core, safe cardio, and HIIT integration"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1 Summary" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DESCRIPTION: Acclimatisation and gentle loading. Short sessions (~30 minutes) at low–moderate intensity; focus on form, pelvic floor, diastasis awareness; light cardio options; anti-flexion core.
      KEY SESSIONS:
        - 3 training days with 2x10–12 reps per exercise on main lifts; RPE ~5.
        - Core: anti-extension/anti-rotation holds and gentle anti-flexion variants.
        - Cardio: optional short, low-impact bouts (walking, cycling, rower) ~5 minutes.
      SCREENING FOCUS:
        - Self-screen diastasis: width/visibility, doming with hook-lying curl, report any separation >2 cm.
        - Pelvic floor check-in: leakage, urge, heaviness with exertion.
        - Pain/ROM check: no increased back or abdominal pain during loads.

    WEEK 2:
      DESCRIPTION: Foundation loading with modest intensity uptick. 35 minutes typical. Introduce light HIIT blocks and cardio variance.
      KEY SESSIONS:
        - 3 sessions: 3x/each main movement + added core holds.
        - HIIT: short intervals (bike or rower) integrated in 1 session per week.
        - Cardio: cycling or spin option; 6 minutes total per session in addition to warmup.
      SCREENING FOCUS:
        - Reassess diastasis symptoms with abdominal loading; document width, doming during loaded carries or flexion attempts.
        - Core control during anti-extension and anti-rotation holds; ensure no bracing-induced doming.
        - Recovery status: energy, sleep, mood; adjust volume if soreness persists.

    WEEK 3:
      DESCRIPTION: Progression with moderate intensity and greater session complexity. Maintain anti-flexion core.
      KEY SESSIONS:
        - 3–4 main sets per exercise; moderate RPE targets ~6.
        - HIIT: 1–2 short blocks if tolerated.
        - Cardio: 8 minutes cumulative per session on chosen modality.
      SCREENING FOCUS:
        - Monitor for signs of diastasis widening or abdominal doming during core work and high-tension movements.
        - Pelvic floor symptoms during exertion; adjust load if leakage or heaviness arises.
        - Gait mechanics during cardio and minimal-impact drills.

    WEEK 4:
      DESCRIPTION: Load tolerance and readiness for ongoing progression; emphasis on safe HIIT and continued cardio variety.
      KEY SESSIONS:
        - 4x main lifts with slight volume uptick; RPE targets ~6.5.
        - Core: sustained anti-extension holds; 30s holds or 12–15 reps of anti-rotation variants.
        - Cardio: low-to-moderate, steady or interval style as tolerated.
      SCREENING FOCUS:
        - Diastasis status: ensure width remains stable or improves; no doming with added load.
        - Pain/functional symptoms: no new pelvis or core pain; monitor for signs of overtraining.
        - Readiness for continued progression beyond week 4; decision to advance running if cleared remains with clinician.

PHASE ALL weeks:
  SCREENING & MONITORING NOTES:
    - Diastasis: track separation width, doming, and functional symptoms at rest and during gentle ab work; document any changes.
    - Pelvic floor: monitor leakage, tremor, or pelvic heaviness during exertion; adjust loading if needed.
    - Core strategy: prioritize anti-flexion, anti-extension, anti-rotation movements; avoid full spinal flexion loading.
    - Jumping: continue to avoid jumping unless cleared by clinician; substitute with step-ups, marching, or low-impact alternatives.
    - Progression guardrails: increase intensity only if form is intact, RPE remains controlled, and screening signs are favorable.
    - Recovery: ensure adequate sleep, nutrition, and manage fatigue; back off if soreness or joint pain increases.

EQUIPMENT
  - Dumbbells for home use; bodyweight options; cardio can be walking, cycling, or rowing.

NOTES:
  - All sessions adhere to canonical exercise names; no jumping until clearance.
  - HIIT is optional and should be introduced only if core stability and diastasis screening remain favorable.
  - If any diastasis widens or symptoms worsen at any point, revert to lower intensity and consult clinician before progressing.
